solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ageing business in fuel beginning to trouble old country

indicators.note: the ageing business is placed within the fuel, as the surface says

parts.note: gas is a fuel
ageing means old
Co is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: the beginning of the word trouble supplies its opening letter

explanation.surface: An old firm deep in the energy trade is starting to bring trouble to a former nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gold Coast was the colonial name of what is now Ghana.
explanation.definitionFit: A former British colony, renamed Ghana at independence in 1957, so it is a country that no longer exists under that name.

clue.text: Sell up partnership before start of Spanish course

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word read from bottom to top

parts.note: to flog is slang for to sell
a link is a connection or partnership

indicators.note: the start of the word Spanish gives its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone cashes in a business partnership before starting a Spanish course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' looks like a class in Spanish, but it is the golfing kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside golf ground is a type of course where the game is played.

clue.text: See 1
Section of jug popular with one sculptor

parts.note: jug is slang for prison, and a cell is one section of it
in means fashionable or popular
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Part of a jug proves popular with a lone sculptor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jug' looks like a pot but is slang for prison. Benvenuto Cellini was an Italian Renaissance sculptor and goldsmith.
explanation.definitionFit: Benvenuto Cellini made the bronze Perseus in Florence, so he is a famous example of a sculptor.

clue.text: A ringing, repeated at start, that might be heard at court

definitions.text: that might be heard at court

indicators.note: the opening letter of the ringing word is doubled at its beginning

parts.note: a peal is a ringing of bells
the first letter of the ringing word, given a second time

explanation.surface: A ringing sound, repeated, that someone in a courtroom might hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeated at start' doubles the first letter of PEAL, giving PPEAL, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: A case taken to a higher court to challenge a verdict is argued before judges there.

clue.text: English tract fell inside widespread delta

indicators.note: the fell word goes within the rearranged letters
the letters of delta are spread out into a new order

parts.note: to fell a tree is to hew it down

explanation.surface: A stretch of English land where a fell lies inside a broad river delta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'widespread' signals the anagram, giving TEALD. 'fell' looks like a hill but is the verb. The Weald lies between the North and South Downs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Weald is a region of south-east England between two chalk ridges, a well-known tract of land.

clue.text: Break up from second grade at end of March?

indicators.note: the grade letter is placed at the end of the march word

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
B is the second grade after A

explanation.surface: A school break-up date, with second-grade pupils finishing at the end of March.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital in 'March' hides the protest march, a demo.
explanation.definitionFit: To demobilise is to disband troops, breaking up a military force after service.

clue.text: Sat, perhaps grabbing seat in old country

indicators.note: the day word takes hold of the seat word, enclosing it

parts.note: Sat is short for Saturday, an example of a day
a seat can be a home, as in a country seat

explanation.surface: Someone sat down, grabbing a seat in a long-gone nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sat' reads as a verb but is the abbreviation for Saturday. Dahomey is the old name of Benin.
explanation.definitionFit: Dahomey was a West African kingdom and then colony, renamed Benin in 1975, so a former nation.

clue.text: Capricious church psychic with fancy lamé clothing

indicators.note: the rearranged fabric wraps around the church and psychic pieces
fancy signals the letters are worked into a decorative new order

parts.note: lamé is a metallic fabric, used for its letters
RC stands for Roman Catholic church
Uri Geller is a famous self-styled psychic

explanation.surface: A fickle churchgoing psychic dressed in showy metallic lamé.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' is the anagram signal, splitting the fabric's letters into two parts that 'clothing' wraps around the rest. Uri Geller is the psychic.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone volatile and unpredictable in mood, like quicksilver, is described as capricious.

clue.text: Old country plain attracts head of sciences in car

indicators.note: the plain word draws the other pieces into itself

parts.note: bland means plain and unremarkable

indicators.note: the first letter goes inside the car word

parts.note: auto is short for automobile, a car

indicators.note: the head of the word sciences is its first letter

explanation.surface: A plain former country draws in the leading science student in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: Basutoland was the colonial name for Lesotho.
explanation.definitionFit: Basutoland was a British protectorate in southern Africa, renamed Lesotho at independence in 1966.

clue.text: "Aim between the lines" suggests tennis expert

indicators.note: the aim word sits between the two line letters

parts.note: L stands for line, so two lines give two Ls
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A coach's advice to aim inside the court lines points to a tennis great.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivan Lendl won eight Grand Slam singles titles.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan Lendl was a world number one player and later a coach, so a master of the racket sport.

clue.text: Statistical data of catering sales at football ground?

definitions.meaning: diagrams showing proportions as slices of a circle
a playful reading: records of how many pies are sold at a match

explanation.surface: Figures on how much food the stadium kiosks sell.
explanation.walkthrough: Pies are classic football-ground food in Britain; the second reading imagines charts of pie sales.
explanation.definitionFit: Circular diagrams divided into slices are a standard way of presenting statistical data.

clue.text: Furious with anonymous sick phoner primarily making breathy sound

indicators.note: primarily means take the first letter of each of the three words

parts.note: irate means furious

explanation.surface: An angry, anonymous caller who is unwell, breathing heavily down the phone.
explanation.walkthrough: An aspirate is the h sound in phonetics.
explanation.definitionFit: In phonetics the term names an h sound, a consonant made by a puff of breath.

clue.text: Flash extremist destroying artist's shed

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a flash

indicators.note: destroying means the artist letters are removed from the extremist word

parts.note: an ultra is an extremist
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A hothead in a flash wrecks a painter's garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like the noun, but it is the verb, as an animal sheds hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals that lose feathers, fur or skin seasonally are said to shed them.

clue.text: Excited oddball startled a lot in old country

parts.note: up can mean excited or worked up
perv is slang for a pervert, an oddball

indicators.note: startled letters jump into a new order

explanation.surface: An excitable weirdo startled plenty of people in a former country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'startled' rearranges A LOT into OLTA. Upper Volta is now Burkina Faso.
explanation.definitionFit: A French West African colony and then republic, renamed Burkina Faso in 1984.

clue.text: Old country discovered through another one mostly

parts.note: per means through, as in by way of

indicators.note: mostly means the old country loses its last letter

parts.note: Siam is another old country, now Thailand

explanation.surface: A former nation discovered by travelling through most of a neighbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Persia is the old name for Iran, and Siam for Thailand.
explanation.definitionFit: Persia was the name used in the West for Iran until 1935, so it is a former name of a country.

clue.text: Reddish-brown fish appearing, son whispers

parts.note: rust is a reddish-brown colour
ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A reddish-brown fish surfaces, and a son murmurs.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft swishing noises, like leaves or silk, can be described as whispers.

clue.text: Theatre poster shows amateur in lead unfavourably

indicators.note: the amateur word goes inside the chemical symbol

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
lay means non-professional, amateur
ill means badly or unfavourably, as in speak ill of

explanation.surface: A theatre poster depicts a non-professional in the lead role, critically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like the star role but is the metal, Pb.
explanation.definitionFit: A printed sheet advertising a theatre production is a poster for the show.

clue.text: Dessert comes with a French-style cream

parts.note: afters is British slang for pudding or dessert
un is French for a

explanation.surface: A dessert served with French-style cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cream' looks like part of the dessert, but it is a skin lotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A soothing lotion applied to skin after sunbathing is a kind of cream.

clue.text: Scottish team favourite disheartened by new Fiesta

indicators.note: new signals the letters are made into a fresh order
disheartened means the middle letters are removed

parts.note: fave is informal for favourite

explanation.surface: A Scottish side's favourite player is dispirited by a new Ford Fiesta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges FIESTA into EASTFI; 'disheartened' cuts AV from FAVE. East Fife is a football club in Methil, Fife.
explanation.definitionFit: East Fife is a Scottish professional football club, so it names a team from Scotland.

clue.text: Old country doctors fill message boards

indicators.note: the doctors fill the space inside the boards word

parts.note: fora is a plural of forum, a message board
MOs are medical officers, doctors

explanation.surface: Doctors in a former country crowd online message boards.
explanation.walkthrough: Formosa is the old name for Taiwan.
explanation.definitionFit: The Portuguese name for Taiwan, widely used in the West until the mid-twentieth century.

clue.text: Old country cottage empty only when renovated

indicators.note: an empty word keeps only its outside letters
renovated signals the word only is rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: An empty cottage in a former country is only habitable once renovated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when renovated' rearranges ONLY into YLON. Ceylon is now Sri Lanka.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceylon was the name of Sri Lanka until 1972, so a former country name.

clue.text: One burrows hard into rocks, tracking and retreating

indicators.note: retreating means everything built so far is read backwards
tracking means following behind the word and
the hard letter goes into the rocks word

parts.note: rocks is slang for ice, as in on the rocks
H is the abbreviation for hard on pencils

explanation.surface: A burrowing creature tunnels into hard rock, tracking prey and then backing off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' gives IHCE; 'tracking' puts it after AND; 'retreating' reverses ANDIHCE.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiny anteater of Australia digs burrows, so it is a creature that burrows.

clue.text: A continental starter with cold filling brought about complaint

indicators.note: brought about means turned round, so the whole is read backwards
the cold letter fills the starter word

parts.note: meze are Mediterranean appetisers
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A European appetiser filled with something cold triggered a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought about' looks like caused, but it reverses AMEZCE. 'complaint' is an ailment, not a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaint can mean a medical condition, and this itchy skin inflammation is one.

clue.text: Soldiers tracking can back GI's bravery

indicators.note: tracking means the soldiers follow behind
back means the can word is read backwards

parts.note: can and lav are both slang for a toilet
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops following a turned-back can show an American soldier's courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'GI's' flags the American spelling, without the u.
explanation.definitionFit: Courage in the face of danger, spelt the American way as a GI would.

clue.text: Religious portrayal in green around chrome building Rector ignored

indicators.note: the green word goes around the rebuilt letters

parts.note: eco means environmentally friendly, green

indicators.note: building signals the remaining letters are assembled anew
ignored means the rector letter is left out

explanation.surface: A religious image in a green, chrome-plated building, with the rector left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored' drops R from CHROME; 'building' rearranges CHOME into CEHOM. Ecce Homo, Latin for behold the man, is a painting of Christ crowned with thorns.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting or sculpture showing Christ crowned with thorns, a common subject in religious art.

clue.text: Country singer mostly seen in American comeback tour

indicators.note: tour means going round, so the American piece encircles the singer
comeback means the American abbreviation is read backwards
mostly means the singer word loses its last letter

parts.note: an alto is a singer

explanation.surface: A country singer, mostly seen on an American comeback tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country singer' looks like one phrase; 'Country' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean island republic is an independent nation.

clue.text: Type of mark that's seen on boxers? Second rib

definitions.text: Type of mark that's seen on boxers?

parts.note: to rib is to tease, to kid

explanation.surface: Some kind of bruise visible on prize fighters, perhaps from a second's broken rib.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxers' are underpants, not fighters; the question mark flags the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A brown streak left in underwear is crude slang for a mark of that sort.

clue.text: Angle at sea holding sack for shellfish

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the sack word inside
at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: to sack is to oust

explanation.surface: An angler at sea holds a sack ready for a catch of seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges ANGLE into LANGE, which holds OUST.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiny lobster, a crustacean, is a kind of shellfish.

clue.text: Legless automaton having beer in middle of vodkas

indicators.note: the beer goes inside the middle letters
the middle of the word vodkas is its central pair of letters

parts.note: ale is beer

explanation.surface: A robot gets legless, mixing beer with vodkas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legless' looks like drunk, which fits the beer and vodkas, but Daleks glide with no legs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Doctor Who villains are robot-like machines moving on a base rather than legs.

clue.text: Lost cat's ear marginally scratched

indicators.note: marginally scratched means the phrase loses its edge letters at each side

explanation.surface: A lost cat whose ear has been slightly scratched.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the first and last letters of CATSEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bewildered or confused is to be all at sea, an idiom for lost.

clue.text: Old country's funny as Alan Davies partly shows

indicators.note: partly means only part of the phrase supplies the letters

explanation.surface: Comedian Alan Davies partly shows off an old country in a funny routine.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Davies is a British comedian. Nyasaland is now Malawi.
explanation.definitionFit: Nyasaland was a British protectorate in central Africa, renamed Malawi in 1964.
